sections.wikitext: "I Gotta Feeling" was written and composed by all the members of [[the Black Eyed Peas]] (credited as [[will.i.am|William Adams]], [[apl.de.ap|Allan Pineda]], [[Taboo (rapper)|Jaime Gomez]], and [[Fergie (singer)|Stacy Ferguson]]) together with French producers [[David Guetta]], Frédéric Riesterer (a.k.a. Fred Rister), both of whom produced the song. Adams provided additional synthesizer work to the song. The song was recorded at Square Prod in Paris, France and [[Metropolis Group|Metropolis Studios]] in London, England, United Kingdom. "I Gotta Feeling" is the second single released from ''[[The E.N.D]]'' (2009). [[Interscope Records]] serviced the song to [[Contemporary hit radio|contemporary hit]] and [[rhythmic crossover]] radios on June 23, 2009, in the United States.<ref name=contemporaryhit>{{cite web|title=R&R :: Going for Adds :: CHR/Top 40 |url=http://gfa.radioandrecords.com/publishGFA/GFANextPage.asp?sDate=06/15/2009&Format=1 |work=Going for Adds |publisher=[[Radio and Records|Radio & Records, Inc.]] |access-date=April 11, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120914123503/http://gfa.radioandrecords.com/publishGFA/GFANextPage.asp?sDate=06%2F15%2F2009&Format=1 |archive-date=September 14, 2012 }}</ref><ref name=fmqb>{{cite web|title=Airplay Archive |url=http://www.fmqb.com/Article.asp?id=69239#29 |work=[[FMQB]] |publisher=Friday Morning Quarterback Album Report, Inc. and Mediaspan Online Services |access-date=April 11, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091101141712/http://www.fmqb.com/Article.asp?id=69239 |archive-date=November 1, 2009}}</ref> In an interview with Annie Reuter of [[Marie Claire]], will.i.am stated that "It's dedicated to all the party people out there in the world that want to go out and party. Times are really hard for a lot of people and you want to give them escape and you want to make them feel good about life, especially at these low points."<ref name=reuter>{{cite web|last=Reuter|first=Annie|title=Black Eyed Peas Talk New Album, Performing on "American Idol" Finale |url=http://www.marieclaire.com/world-reports/opinion/black-eyed-peas-interview|work=[[Marie Claire]]|publisher=Hearst Communications, Inc.|access-date=April 11, 2012|date=May 19, 2009}}</ref>

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext: The song is an uptempo [[dance-pop]] song that runs a length of four minutes and 49 seconds and runs at a tempo of 128 [[beats per minute]] in the key of [[G major]]. It follows in the inspirational dance-pop theme of ''The E.N.D'', being built upon the heavy use of [[Auto-Tune]] and futuristic synthesizers while running through a tick-tock rhythm.<ref name=bush/><ref name=balls/><ref name=lamb/> The song begins in a restrained fashion, then moves into a throbbing dance beat that changes patterns so that at least one reviewer thought it shifted tempos,<ref name=balls/> although in fact the tempo does not change at all, suggesting the use of a click track in recording. It contains electronic influences. Ann Powers of ''Los Angeles Times'' noted the song's similarities to [[Five Stairsteps]]' song "[[O-o-h Child]]", writing that it emulates the song's "use of a repetitive, warm vocal line to signify a good mood coming on."<ref name=powers/> According to Jimmy Iovine of the [[Interscope Geffen A&M]] label group, the melody was inspired by the [[U2]] song "[[I'll Go Crazy If I Don't Go Crazy Tonight]]": "I sent will.i.am over to the studio to do some remixes on I'll Go Crazy. He works on them for two weeks, comes back and writes I Gotta Feeling. The chords are U2 chords, 100 per cent. Will even told them."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://uk.omg.yahoo.com/news/am-borrowed-melody-u2-song-083815131.html |title=will.i.am borrowed melody from U2 song - Yahoo! omg! UK |publisher=Uk.omg.yahoo.com |date=April 20, 2012 |access-date=June 8, 2012}}</ref> The lyric "Fill up my cup, [[mazel tov]]" was written by will.i.am to follow the same pattern as "Psycho killer, qu'est-ce que c'est?" in the [[Talking Heads]] song "[[Psycho Killer]]": four syllables in English followed by three syllables in another language.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Platt |first=Daci |date=2026-07-16 |title=Yes, "I Gotta Feeling" By the Black Eyed Peas Has a Jewish Backstory |url=https://www.kveller.com/yes-i-gotta-feeling-by-the-black-eyed-peas-has-a-jewish-backstory/ |access-date=2026-09-09 |website=Kveller |language=en}}</ref>

Ben Westhoff of Las Vegas Weekly dismissed the song as a blend of house, electro and dancehall beats that did not work compared to songs on The E.N.D like "Imma Be" and "One Tribe", while others like David Balls (a writer for Digital Spy) considered the song "as every bit as quirky as its predecessor ("Boom Boom Pow")". Balls compared it to Girls Aloud's "Biology", writing that they sound like a collection of musical ideas "that only makes sense after a few listens." Another writer for Digital Spy, Nick Levine, praised "I Gotta Feeling" and "Rock That Body" as ace collaborations with French disc jockey David Guetta. Music critics like John Bush of All Music Guide and Andy Gill of The Independent labeled it as one of the album's best tracks. Ann Powers wrote a positive review about "I Gotta Feeling", noting that "the Peas do let in some human sweetness and light" on the song and that it uses "a repetitive, warm vocal line to signify a good mood coming on."

Mike Schiller, a writer for PopMatters, found the song to be irresistible, writing that it "is one of those dance tunes that's impossible to hate thanks to something like good natured naïveté". In his review of the album for Stuff.co.nz, Chris Schultz dismissed the lyrics, writing that they were the worst since Flo Rida's "Right Round".

The Observer-Dispatch writer David T. Farr praised the song as "the summer track of 2009", writing that "It's one of those songs you grasp onto right away and crank up as the beat goes on, even the first time you hear it (guilty as charged)." Will Hines of Consequence of Sound shared similar feelings about "I Gotta Feeling", defining it as "chart baiting". Guy Blackman, a writer for The Age, labeled "I Gotta Feeling" and "Boom Boom Pow" as further dumbed-down dance-pop songs. Bill Lamb of About.com gave the song a four-star rating, praising it for the difference of style from previous releases by the Black Eyed Peas and as a great summer song with a feel-good mood, but he criticized the lack of lyrical depth and constant use of Auto-Tune. sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext:
"I Gotta Feeling" followed in the international success of ''[[The E.N.D]]''{{'}}s lead single "[[Boom Boom Pow]]". In the United States, the song debuted on the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] at number two, behind "Boom Boom Pow", prompted by sales of 249,000 downloads.<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Ben-Yehuda|first=Ayala|title=Black Eyed Peas Take Top Two Slots On Billboard Hot 100|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/268343/black-eyed-peas-take-top-two-slots-on-billboard-hot-100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref> The song held at number two for another week before rising to the top position on the chart.<ref>{{cite web|title='Feeling' is No. 1 on U.S. record chart |url=http://www.upi.com/Entertainment_News/2009/07/09/Feeling-is-No-1-on-US-record-chart/UPI-49711247180220/|work=UPI|publisher=United Press International, Inc.|access-date=April 13, 2012|date=July 9, 2009}}</ref> On July 30, 2009, it was reported that the song, along with "Boom Boom Pow", helped earn the Black Eyed Peas the longest run at number one on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 by a duo or group (17 weeks).<ref>{{cite magazine|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/267898/black-eyed-peas-set-billboard-hot-100-record|title=Black Eyed Peas Set Billboard Hot 100 Record|last1=Ben-Yehuda|first1=Ayala|last2=Caulfield|first2=Keith|date=July 30, 2009|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=April 13, 2012|last3=Pietroluongo|first3=Silvio}}</ref> The song stayed at number one on the chart for a total of fourteen weeks before being unseated by [[Jay Sean]]'s "[[Down (Jay Sean song)|Down]]".<ref name=pietroluongo>{{cite magazine|last=Pietroluongo|first=Silvio|title=Jay Sean Sends Peas Packing From Hot 100 Penthouse|url=http://www.billboard.com/articles/news/267156/jay-sean-sends-peas-packing-from-hot-100-penthouse|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine|title=Hot 100 – October 17, 2009|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/2009-10-17/hot-100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref> The song, together with "Boom Boom Pow", earned the group a total of 26 consecutive weeks atop the Hot 100 chart while also earning them their longest running single on the chart, with a total of 56 weeks logged.<ref name=pietroluongo/><ref name=billboardcharts/>

"I Gotta Feeling" also peaked at number one on several other ''Billboard'' charts, including [[Hot Digital Songs]], [[Mainstream Top 40]], and [[Radio Songs (chart)|Radio Songs]].<ref name=billboardcharts>{{cite magazine|title=I Gotta Feeling – Billboard Chart History|url={{BillboardURLbyName|artist=the black eyed peas|chart=all}}|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref> It was the group's second single to sell over 6 million downloads in the United States, and was certified 7× Platinum on August 25, 2010 by the [[Recording Industry Association of America]] (RIAA), signifying sales of over 7 million units. It was the first song to reach sales of over 6 million (November 25, 2010), 7 million (March 20, 2011), 8 million (June 24, 2012), and 9 million (June 7, 2019).<ref name="yahoo_may2013">{{cite news|url=http://music.yahoo.com/blogs/chart-watch/chart-watch-extra-itunes-turns-10-213705272.html|title=Chart Watch Extra: iTunes Turns 10|last=Grein|first=Paul|date=May 1, 2013|work=Yahoo Music (Chart Watch)|access-date=May 4, 2013}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|number=1137046191378579456|user=HITSDD|title=Ahead of its 10th anniversary, The...|date=June 7, 2019}}</ref> It also earned the accolade of being the best digital seller in history.<ref name="mtv.com"/>

In Canada, the song debuted on the [[Canadian Hot 100]] at number two behind "Boom Boom Pow", similar to its beginning run in the United States, on the week ending June 27, 2009.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Canadian Hot 100 – June 27, 2009|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/2009-06-27/canadian-hot-100|magazine=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref> The next week, it rose to number one following a surge in airplay, where it maintained that position for 16 consecutive weeks, setting the record for longest run at number one since the chart's inception in 2007.<ref>{{cite magazine|title=Canadian Hot 100 – July 4, 2009|url=http://www.billboard.com/charts/2009-07-04/canadian-hot-100|magazine=Billboard|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref><ref name=internationalchartsigf>{{cite web|title=The Black Eyed Peas – I Gotta Feeling|url=http://acharts.us/song/44000|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=April 13, 2012}}</ref> The song was present on the chart for a total of 76 weeks, setting the record for longest stay on the chart.<ref name=billboardcharts/><ref name=internationalchartsigf/> The song was certified Diamond by Music Canada for sales of over 800,000 digital downloads.<ref name="Canada Certified Diamond">{{cite web|title=Gold Platinum Database|url=https://musiccanada.com/GPSearchResult.aspx?st=I%20Gotta%20Feeling&ica=False&sa=Black%20Eyed%20Peas&sl=&smt=0&sat=-1&ssd=5/1/2007&ssb=Artist|work=[[Music Canada]]|access-date=April 16, 2012}}</ref>

"I Gotta Feeling" fared similarly in international markets. The song had a slower rise in the United Kingdom, where it debuted at number 70 on the week ending June 20, 2009.<ref>{{cite web|title=UK Singles Top 75 – June 20, 2009|url=http://acharts.us/uk_singles_top_75/2009/25|work=aCharts|publisher=acharts.us|access-date=April 16, 2012}}</ref> It quickly picked up momentum, moving into the top five in its fifth week on the chart. On the week ending August 8, 2009, the song peaked at number one, becoming the group's third number one and staying there for two non-consecutive weeks.<ref>{{cite web|title=2009 Top 40 Official UK Singles Archive – August 8, 2009|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/20090802/7501/|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=April 16, 2012|date=August 8, 2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=2009 Top 40 Official UK Singles Archive – August 22, 2009|url=https://www.officialcharts.com/charts/singles-chart/20090816/7501/|work=[[Official Charts Company]]|access-date=April 16, 2012|date=August 8, 2009}}</ref> "I Gotta Feeling" held within the top ten for 16 consecutive weeks and lasted on the chart for a total of 76 weeks. "I Gotta Feeling" peaked at number one in countries including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Italy, The Netherlands, and New Zealand.<ref name=internationalchartsigf/> The song reached top five peak positions in Finland, France, Norway, and Spain.<ref name=internationalchartsigf/> It has sold over seven million units worldwide in 2009 and an additional six million in 2010, as reported by the IFPI.<ref name=ifpione>{{cite web|title=Digital Music Sales Around the World|url=http://www.ifpi.com/content/library/dmr2010.pdf|work=[[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]]|publisher=IFPI|access-date=April 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322183800/http://www.ifpi.com/content/library/dmr2010.pdf|archive-date=March 22, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=ifpitwo>{{cite web|title=IFPI publishes Digital Music Report 2011|url=http://www.ifpi.com/content/section_resources/dmr2011.html|work=[[International Federation of the Phonographic Industry]]|publisher=IFPI|access-date=April 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111011144923/http://www.ifpi.com/content/section_resources/dmr2011.html|archive-date=October 11, 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref>
sections.text:
"I Gotta Feeling" followed in the international success of The E.N.D{{'}}s lead single "Boom Boom Pow". In the United States, the song debuted on the Billboard Hot 100 at number two, behind "Boom Boom Pow", prompted by sales of 249,000 downloads. The song held at number two for another week before rising to the top position on the chart. On July 30, 2009, it was reported that the song, along with "Boom Boom Pow", helped earn the Black Eyed Peas the longest run at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 by a duo or group (17 weeks). The song stayed at number one on the chart for a total of fourteen weeks before being unseated by Jay Sean's "Down". The song, together with "Boom Boom Pow", earned the group a total of 26 consecutive weeks atop the Hot 100 chart while also earning them their longest running single on the chart, with a total of 56 weeks logged.

"I Gotta Feeling" also peaked at number one on several other Billboard charts, including Hot Digital Songs, Mainstream Top 40, and Radio Songs. It was the group's second single to sell over 6 million downloads in the United States, and was certified 7× Platinum on August 25, 2010 by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), signifying sales of over 7 million units. It was the first song to reach sales of over 6 million (November 25, 2010), 7 million (March 20, 2011), 8 million (June 24, 2012), and 9 million (June 7, 2019). It also earned the accolade of being the best digital seller in history.

In Canada, the song debuted on the Canadian Hot 100 at number two behind "Boom Boom Pow", similar to its beginning run in the United States, on the week ending June 27, 2009. The next week, it rose to number one following a surge in airplay, where it maintained that position for 16 consecutive weeks, setting the record for longest run at number one since the chart's inception in 2007. The song was present on the chart for a total of 76 weeks, setting the record for longest stay on the chart. The song was certified Diamond by Music Canada for sales of over 800,000 digital downloads.

"I Gotta Feeling" fared similarly in international markets. The song had a slower rise in the United Kingdom, where it debuted at number 70 on the week ending June 20, 2009. It quickly picked up momentum, moving into the top five in its fifth week on the chart. On the week ending August 8, 2009, the song peaked at number one, becoming the group's third number one and staying there for two non-consecutive weeks. "I Gotta Feeling" held within the top ten for 16 consecutive weeks and lasted on the chart for a total of 76 weeks. The song was certified 5× Platinum by the British Phonographic Industry on December 27, 2024 for sales and streams of 3 million units. "I Gotta Feeling" became the first song to sell over one million units based solely on the strength of digital downloads, and has sold over 1.44 million copies in the United Kingdom as of May 2014. In Ireland, the song peaked at number one and held that position for 12 non-consecutive weeks, falling to number two on the week of August 27, 2009, after six weeks in the top position. It rose to number one the following week and held that position for another six weeks. In Sweden, the song debuted on the chart at number 36 on the week ending July 19, 2009. It quickly entered the top ten and peaked at number one in its seventh week on the chart. "I Gotta Feeling" maintained its position there for eight consecutive weeks and stayed present on the charts for a total of 87 weeks. The single was certified double platinum for sales of 40,000 units. In Germany, the song debuted on the chart at number seven and rose to number three two weeks later.

"I Gotta Feeling" peaked at number one in countries including Australia, Austria, Belgium, Denmark, Italy, The Netherlands, and New Zealand. The song reached top five peak positions in Finland, France, Norway, and Spain. It has sold over seven million units worldwide in 2009 and an additional six million in 2010, as reported by the IFPI.

The video starts with scenes in [[Hollywood Blvd.]], then shows [[will.i.am]] combing his hair and [[Fergie (singer)|Fergie]] putting on make-up while wearing lingerie. It also shows [[Taboo (rapper)|Taboo]] checking his messages on Dipdive and [[apl.de.ap]] checking his text messages. Then, it cuts to a party as the first verse starts. The video ends with a large sign with human-sized letters that reads "The E.N.D".
